title: Cohort Playback latency explorer: route + request-shape with streaming vs non-streaming breakdown
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a new console explorer called "Cohort Playback" that makes it easy to investigate tail latency by model route and request shape, with explicit comparisons between streaming and non-streaming IO modes. This ticket covers instrumentation hooks, metric and log pipeline updates, and the dashboard UX. Key goals: (1) surface p50/p95/p99 splits by model route and by request-shape cohorts (conversation length, prompt tokens, multi-turn vs single-turn), (2) show streaming vs non-streaming breakdown side-by-side with per-token streaming boundary markers, (3) enable a sampled timeline replay for representative requests within a cohort so engineers can inspect KV-cache warm/cold behavior, batching delays, and kernel scheduling stalls.
acceptance_criteria: Metrics: p50/p95/p99 available for each model route and each request-shape cohort with separate series for streaming and non-streaming IO modes
Tracing: streaming boundary hooks added to runtime traces (stream-start, stream-chunk, stream-end) and propagated to trace IDs for correlation with logs/metrics

Dashboard: Cohort Playback view in Console with filters for route, model, request-shape buckets, and toggle for streaming vs non-streaming. Includes timeline replay UI that can load sampled request events and annotate KV cache state and batch boundaries
Sampling: timeline replay sampled for at least 1% of requests per route or min 50 req/day per route, persisted for 7 days for playback
Alerting: example alert rule template included that fires when route p95 (24h) increases > 2x baseline or streaming/non-streaming p95 delta exceeds 100ms
Performance: additional tracing tags and logging add <2% CPU overhead on hot serving path in perf test environment
tasks: Design: finalize Cohort Playback mockups and UX flows (link in links)
Instrumentation: add streaming boundary trace hooks and tag request_shape, kv_cache_state, batch_id
Metrics pipeline: add request-shape label to token latency histograms and expose streaming boolean
Logs: enrich access logs with io_mode and request_cohort fields and update logparser
Dashboard: implement backend query layer and frontend view in Console, wire pagination and replay sample fetch
Testing: run perf and SLO rollout in staging, validate overhead and correctness
Docs: write runbook and how-to for investigating cohort regressions
